title: Delete the Middle Node of a Linked List
statement: You receive `head`, the first node of a singly linked list holding `n` nodes. Remove the node sitting at 0-based position `⌊n / 2⌋` (for `n` = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 that is position 0, 1, 1, 2, 2) and return the head of the list that remains. If the list had a single node, nothing is left, so return `null` (an empty list).
constraints: The list has between 1 and 10^5 nodes.
notes:
## Intuition

The node to remove sits at position `⌊n / 2⌋`, and to unlink it we need the node just before it. Counting the nodes first and then walking again works, but a fast pointer that moves two steps for every one step of a slow pointer finds that spot in a single pass: when the fast pointer runs out of list, the slow one has covered half the distance.

## Approach

1. If the list has one node, removing it leaves nothing, so return `null`.
2. Start `slow` at the head and `fast` two nodes ahead. This head start makes `slow` stop one node *before* the middle.
3. While `fast` and `fast.next` both exist, advance `slow` by one and `fast` by two.
4. Unlink the middle with `slow.next = slow.next.next`.
5. Return `head`, which never changes when `n >= 2`.

## Example 1, step by step

The list is `1 → 3 → 4 → 7 → 1 → 2 → 6` (n = 7, middle index 3).

- Start: `slow` at index 0 (value 1), `fast` at index 2 (value 4).
- `fast` has a next node: `slow` moves to index 1 (3), `fast` to index 4 (1).
- `fast` has a next node: `slow` moves to index 2 (4), `fast` to index 6 (6).
- `fast.next` is `null`, so the loop stops. `slow.next` is index 3 (value 7); skipping it gives `[1,3,4,1,2,6]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): `fast` walks the list once, two nodes per step.
- Space: O(1): only two pointers are kept.

## Pitfalls

- A one-node list must return `null`; `head.next.next` would crash there.
- Starting both pointers at `head` lands `slow` *on* the middle, which is one node too far to unlink it.
- For even `n` the middle is the upper one (index 2 of 4), so check the loop on `n = 2` and `n = 4`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `head` | first node of the list, also the returned head |
| `slow` | moves one node per step; ends just before the middle |
| `fast` | moves two nodes per step; its end marks when to stop |

narration.2: A list with a single node has that node as its middle.
narration.3: Removing it leaves an empty list.
narration.5: The slow pointer starts at the head.
narration.6: The fast pointer starts two nodes ahead so slow will stop just before the middle.
narration.7: Keep going while fast can still take two more steps.
narration.9: Fast advances two nodes, covering twice the distance.
narration.11: Slow is right before the middle, so skip over the middle node to remove it.
narration.12: The head is unchanged; return it.
